sentences.text: Xinjiangtitan possesses the longest complete neck ever discovered for any animal, measuring nearly 15 meters with all 18 vertebrae present.
This giant is diagnosed by traits including a ventral keel on the penultimate cervical vertebra, elongated cervical vertebrae, a specific sacricostal yoke structure, and an extremely robust femur.
The type specimen of Xinjiangtitan shanshanesis was discovered in 2012 by a joint expedition of Jilin University, Shenyang Normal University, and the Xinjiang Geological Survey Institute.

The generic name Xinjiangtitan is derived from the region of Xinjiang and the Greek word for giant, titan, while the specific name shanshanesis is derived from the county of Shanshan, named after the ancient Shanshan Kingdom.
The fossil was originally thought to be from the Late Jurassic Qigu Formation but is now assigned to the Middle Jurassic Qiketai Formation.
Phylogenetic analysis places Xinjiangtitan as the sister taxon of Mamenchisaurus.
Xinjiangtitan shares derived characters with diplodocids, such as a prominent ambiens process of the pubis, a relatively short hind limb, and a caudomedially developed fourth trochanter on the femur.
Xinjiangtitan lived during the Middle Jurassic in what is now northwestern China, approximately 165 to 164 million years ago during the Callovian stage.
The time range for Xinjiangtitan is estimated from the Bathonian to the Tithonian, spanning from 168.2 to 143.1 million years ago.
